ud5.6:3.2: Seated to one side, the layman Soṇa of the Sharp Ears said to Venerable Mahākaccāna,
ud5.6:4.1: “Sir, while I was in private retreat this thought came to my mind,
ud5.6:4.2: ‘As I understand Master Mahākaccāna’s teachings, it’s not easy for someone living at home to lead the spiritual life utterly full and pure, like a polished shell.
ud5.6:4.3: Why don’t I shave off my hair and beard, dress in ocher robes, and go forth from lay life to homelessness?’
ud5.6:6.2: For a second time, Mahākaccāna said to the layman Soṇa of the Sharp Ears,
ud5.6:6.3: “It’s hard to lead the spiritual life as long as you live, eating in one part of the day and sleeping alone.
ud5.6:6.4: Come now, Soṇa, while remaining a layperson just as you are, devote yourself to the instructions of the Buddhas, leading the spiritual life at suitable times, eating in one part of the day and sleeping alone.”
ud5.6:6.5: For a second time, Soṇa’s aspiration to go forth died down.
ud5.6:7.5: Seated to one side, the layman Soṇa of the Sharp Ears said to Venerable Mahākaccāna,

ud5.6:8.3: Why don’t I shave off my hair and beard, dress in ocher robes, and go forth from lay life to homelessness?’
ud5.6:11.2: Seated to one side, Venerable Soṇa said to Venerable Mahākaccāna,
ud5.6:12.1: “Sir, while I was in private retreat this thought came to my mind,
ud5.6:12.2: ‘I have not personally seen the Buddha. I have only heard reports that
ud5.6:12.3: that Blessed One is like this or like that.’
ud5.6:12.4: If my mentor allows, I should go to see that Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.”
